Sheet.title: Dials
Sheet.name: Name
Sheet.noRuleset: Without a ruleset this dial accepts nothing.
Sheet.toneHint: What this dial is, drawn as the colour of its rim. It attaches no rule: a threat may still take positive slices, which is what the accepted signs below decide.
Sheet.closingHint: The last segment accepts nothing else. A dial nobody can close with it stays one short.
Sheet.stateHint: Prepared and Hidden both drop every player's permission, so the dial stops reaching their client at all. Bringing it back into play restores exactly what you had granted.

hudEnabled.name: Show the dials panel
hudEnabled.hint: Anchored panel listing the dials you can see. Drag it by its grip bar, fold it with the chevron. Turning this off hides it entirely.

trackerMode.name: Combat tracker
trackerMode.hint: Either dials share the tracker with the encounter, as a second tab, or they take it over entirely — for a table that never rolls initiative.

defaultSize.name: New dial: size
defaultSize.hint: How many segments a freshly created dial is divided into.

defaultRuleset.name: New dial: ruleset
defaultRuleset.hint: Which system's categories a freshly created dial plays by. Without one it accepts nothing.

defaultState.name: New dial: state
defaultState.hint: Prepared keeps a new dial out of play, and out of the players' clients, until you bring it in.

defaultOnComplete.name: New dial: once complete
defaultOnComplete.hint: What a freshly created dial does to its slices when it fills up.

defaultCelebration.name: New dial: celebration
defaultCelebration.hint: How loudly a freshly created dial lands when it fills up.

Hud.close: Hide the panel (bring it back from the module settings)

Picker.noCategories: This dial has no category to place.
